text:
tara: Heads-up: seeing p99 token latency creep + a handful of OOM-ish allocation fails on dedicated pools in us-central around 15:30 UTC. pattern looks like bursty tenant churn on specific racks.
ops-bot: [ALERT] dedicated-pool-degradation us-central 15:30-15:42 (p99 +12ms, alloc-fail 1.8%)
liam: could be noisy neighbor at rack NIC level. last week we saw similar with driver 510.x and small journals. any packet drops on the top-of-rack?
tara: telemetry shows elevated retransmits on tor-12 and tor-13, and a few hosts reporting NVLINK errors concurrently.
anya: if NVLINK+tor flaps align, shared GPU slices will suffer. recommended quick mitigation: enable per-tenant burst circuit-breaker to stop new fractional slices landing on impacted hosts.
marco: can we do a soft quarantine for tenants with > 200 allocs/min and recent high retry rates? i can add a label to the allocator that prevents colocating their fractional slices with other high-risk tenants.
zoe: +1. also add NIC egress shaping for that rack as a temporary limiter so KV/cache thrash doesn't cascade. we don't want to fully eject traffic — just dampen.
liam: sketch for circuit-breaker rule:
```
match: { region: us-central, tor: [tor-12,tor-13] }
action: {
  block_new_fractional_allocs: true,
  mark_host_state: "soft-quarantine",
  notify: [eng-infra-oncall, quota-team]
  window_sec: 120
  threshold: { alloc_fail_pct: 0.5, net_retransmits: 100 }
}
```
tara: timeline: add circuit-breaker canary on tor-12 for 2 min, monitor p99 and alloc_success. if p99 drops back to baseline and alloc_fails decrease, widen to tor-13.
anya: operational note: this will increase dedicated spill to other racks/regions. consider a fallback policy to route fractional requests to reserved warm-pools first. that keeps locality and avoids cross-region egress.
marco: warm-pool fallback is doable quickly. i'll patch the allocator priority: 1) reserved warm-pool in same az, 2) local other rack, 3) remote az.
zoe: telemetry/alerts to wire: per-host alloc_fail_rate, kv_cache_miss_rate, net_retransmits, nvlink_errs, fractional_alloc_placement_count. add synthetic warm-pool hit-rate test so we can detect cold-cache regressions immediately.
liam: also flagging cost implication: if we divert to remote azs we may hit inter-az egress for some tenants. need a quick pricing sign-off for the incident.
tara: i'll loop in pricing and solutions with a one-liner: "probable temporary shift to warm-pool fallback may add inter-az egress for non-SLA tenants". keep SLA-tagged tenants pinned unless absolutely necessary.
ops-bot: [INFO] incident 12567 created: "us-central-tor-network-noise" assignees: eng-infra oncall, netops
marco: action items: (1) enable circuit-breaker canary on tor-12 (liam) (2) implement warm-pool fallback priority (marco) (3) add egress/cost heads-up to pricing (tara) (4) short-lived NIC egress shaping on tor-12 (zoe) (5) monitor auto-rollback if p99 > baseline +40ms or alloc_fail_rate rises.
anya: one-more-safety: add a per-tenant fairness token-bucket so a single tenant can't burst-claim many fractional slices in <30s. threshold: 5 slices/30s by default, tunable per-tier.
liam: good idea. i'll land the token-bucket on staging and wire `allocator.token_consumption` metric.
tara: ok rolling canary in 5m. i'll post dashboards and brief status updates here. keep customer-impact comms ready if we need to expand to broader fallback.
zoe: leaving a short rollback plan: disable circuit-breaker, remove soft-quarantine label, revert warm-pool routing — all via incident runbook -> rollback step 1.
ops-bot: [INFO] circuit-breaker canary applied: tor-12 window 120s -> action=soft-quarantine (tag=cb-2025-08-17)
